slug: 2021-09-13 The burden of recording and reporting health data in primary health care facilities in five low- and lower-middle income countries

facts.fact: A WHO-led five-country study (Siyam et al., fieldwork 2016-2017, 16 public PHC facilities in Nigeria) found facilities tally paper registers onto paper monthly reporting forms (13 in use in Nigeria, about 10 hours a month) submitted to the district management office, where the data are entered into the district management information system.
facts.system: Routine health information system (RHIS/HMIS) with district management information system

facts.fact: The study states that none of the selected PHC facilities had electronic data collection in place: 0 of the 16 randomly selected public PHC facilities visited in Nigeria (12 health centres, 3 health posts, 1 maternal and child health clinic; four districts), a sample and not a national count, fieldwork 2016-2017.
facts.system: Routine health information system (RHIS/HMIS) with district management information system

facts.fact: Patient recording in all 16 Nigerian public PHC facilities visited in 2016-2017 was on paper registers (Nigeria has 15 registers for HIV alone), and the authors state none of the selected facilities had an electronic system; a sample of 16 facilities in four districts, not a statement about hospitals.
facts.system: Paper facility registers (no electronic patient record)

systems.system: Routine health information system (RHIS/HMIS) with district management information system
systems.country_label: National HMIS / RHIS; district management information system (DMIS)
systems.tiers: PHC facilities (health centres, health posts) report on paper to the district office, where data are keyed
